title: Planning policy undermines UK’s nature goals | Science
content: The UK government has been a vocal advocate for biodiversity conservation and has made ambitious national commitments on biodiversity protection and recovery, including the protection of 30% of UK land, seas, and freshwater by 2030 (1). However, recent and proposed changes to planning policy in England threaten progress toward the UK’s biodiversity targets. England should commit to its environmental goals, which present mutual benefits for its biodiversity, economy, and society (1).
